kept.title: Insecure CI/CD Configuration for npm Publishing
kept.description: The `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml` uses 'npm stage publish', which is a non-standard and potentially dangerous command if relying on untrusted registry configurations or insecure package pre-publish hooks.
steps_to_exploit: Create a malicious release on GitHub
Trigger the publish workflow
The workflow upgrades to latest npm and executes the stage process, potentially running arbitrary code defined in package lifecycle scripts
kept.impact: Account compromise or distribution of malicious packages to the public npm registry.

kept.title: Unsafe child process execution in benchmark scripts
kept.description: benchmark/index.js uses 'spawn' to execute files from the current directory. Since 'fileNames' comes from readdirSync, any file in the benchmark folder is treated as executable code.
steps_to_exploit: Place a malicious file ending in .js in the benchmark directory
Run the benchmark script
The benchmark harness executes the attacker-controlled script with the same privileges as the node process
kept.impact: Remote code execution on the machine running the benchmarks.

kept.title: Disablement of SSL Verification in CI
kept.description: The CI pipeline explicitly disables SSL certificate verification when installing dependencies on older Node.js versions.
steps_to_exploit: Perform a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack during a CI run on Node 0.10
Intercept the npm registry request
Inject malicious code into the dependencies being installed
kept.impact: CI/CD pipeline compromise; supply chain attack.

kept.title: Arbitrary code execution via test environment
kept.description: The test harness in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` modifies the environment and installs external dependencies dynamically, creating an insecure build environment.
steps_to_exploit: Target the repository during a PR
Ensure the PR triggers dependency installation on an older node version
Leverage the lack of integrity verification in the dynamic install process
kept.impact: Injection of unauthorized code into the test/build pipeline.

kept.title: Unsafe usage of 'eval'-like constructs in benchmarks
kept.description: Benchmark files use strings for the 'fn' property in the benchmark suite, which are evaluated by the 'benchmark' library, posing a risk if strings are modified.
steps_to_exploit: Modify the source file to include malicious payload in the string
Run the benchmark test suite
The 'benchmark' library executes the string as code
kept.impact: Arbitrary code execution during local performance testing.

kept.title: Dependency risk in CI workflows
kept.description: The workflows use hardcoded git commit SHAs for actions, but the build logic itself (npm install) is vulnerable to supply chain attacks due to missing lockfiles.
steps_to_exploit: Wait for a dependency to be hijacked
Trigger a CI run
The CI environment pulls the malicious version of the dependency
kept.impact: Infiltration of malicious code into the development lifecycle.

kept.title: Insufficient validation of IP ranges
kept.description: The library allows arbitrary string inputs to compile into trust lists. While validation exists, it relies on complex parsing logic that might be bypassed.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a specifically crafted string to the compile function
Attempt to include overlapping or private subnets that were not intended to be trusted
kept.impact: Misconfiguration leading to bypass of IP-based security controls.

kept.title: Insecure Shell execution in CI
kept.description: Usage of `shell: bash -eo pipefail -l {0}` in GitHub Actions allows for shell injection if inputs are ever sourced from external events.
steps_to_exploit: Manipulate a GitHub event payload to include shell metacharacters
Trigger the CI workflow
kept.impact: Remote code execution within the CI runner.

kept.title: Use of deprecated and vulnerable node versions in CI
kept.description: The CI matrix tests against extremely old, EOL node versions, increasing the attack surface of the test environment.
steps_to_exploit: Exploit a known vulnerability in the Node.js 0.10 environment while it is running on the runner
kept.impact: Sandbox escape or compromise of the CI runner.

kept.title: Missing integrity checks in CI coverage merge
kept.description: The coverage merge process blindly trusts files found via `find` and `xargs` to execute `lcov`.
steps_to_exploit: Inject a malicious file named lcov.info into the coverage directory
Run the workflow
The shell command will execute against the malicious file
kept.impact: Potential execution of malicious scripts during coverage report generation.

evidence.quote: run: find ./coverage -name lcov.info -exec printf '-a %q\n' {} \; | xargs lcov -o ./lcov.info

code_refs.quote: run: find ./coverage -name lcov.info -exec printf '-a %q\n' {} \; | xargs lcov -o ./lcov.info

kept.title: Potentially unsafe path joining in benchmarks
kept.description: The use of `path.join(__dirname, fileName)` where `fileName` is derived from filesystem listing can lead to path traversal if the directory contains symbolic links or unusual entries.
steps_to_exploit: Create a symlink pointing outside the current directory
Run benchmark/index.js
kept.impact: Arbitrary file execution/read access within the scope of the process.

kept.title: Unfiltered input passed to TypeError constructor
kept.description: Passing external inputs directly into error messages can lead to log injection or information disclosure.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a specially crafted IP string
Trigger the validation error
kept.impact: Injection of malicious sequences into application logs.

evidence.quote: throw new TypeError('invalid range on address: ' + note)

code_refs.quote: throw new TypeError('invalid range on address: ' + note)

kept.title: Lack of version pinning for devDependencies
kept.description: Dependencies in package.json allow minor version updates, which could pull in malicious code.
steps_to_exploit: Wait for a devDependency to release a compromised update
Run npm install
kept.impact: Compromise of the local development environment.

kept.title: Insecure default configuration for file persistence in Actions
kept.description: The workflow uses 'persist-credentials: false' which is good, but doesn't explicitly restrict scope.
steps_to_exploit: An attacker with read access to the repo can modify workflows to exfiltrate secrets if not strictly isolated.

kept.title: Weak validation logic for subnet parsing
kept.description: The function uses regex for digit validation but parses integers without sufficient checks on the result.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a string that satisfies the regex but exceeds integer limits
kept.impact: Logic error that could lead to incorrect IP range matching.
